key_insight: LUCQUE introduces a large, comprehensively annotated lung cancer screening dataset from Québec to support more reliable evaluation of AI tools. It aims to make independent assessment more reproducible and comparable.
problem_solved: AI evaluation in lung cancer screening has relied on private or fragmented public datasets, with inconsistent access to clinical data and expert nodule annotations.
method: Build a dataset from low-dose CT lung cancer screening in Québec.
Provide comprehensive annotations to address gaps in existing evaluation resources.
Establish a shared basis for evaluating and comparing AI screening tools.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, LUCQUE could support more consistent benchmarking and independent validation of lung cancer screening models. The supplied abstract is truncated, so dataset size, access conditions, and evaluation results are not confirmed.
visual_elements: Low-dose CT lung image with highlighted nodules to illustrate the screening task.
Pipeline diagram: Québec screening scans → annotated dataset → AI evaluation.
Side-by-side comparison of fragmented evaluation resources and LUCQUE's comprehensive dataset approach.
Icons representing reproducibility, comparability, and independent assessment.
paper_title: LUCQUE: A lung cancer screening dataset from Québec for reliable AI evaluation
paper_authors: Johanna Topalis, Yannick Lemaréchal, Gabriel Couture, Hanife Ersay, Loran Nas
